# Workflow directory

`reusable-app-ci.yml` is the central application-facing workflow. It declares only `workflow_call`; application repositories call it through thin workflows and pass named inputs plus the required `SONAR_TOKEN` secret.

`reusable-app-ci.yml` also contains the opt-in publisher job. Setting `publish_image: true` requests the container build and scan and publishes the image only after every required CI and security gate passes. Caller permissions must allow the complete called workflow, including the pinned OSV workflow and publisher. The workflow contract documents the required scopes and each job's narrower permissions.

`reusable-app-cd.yml` handles Node application ZIP deployment and post-deployment verification in Azure App Service. The sample caller validates `pull_request` events `opened`, `synchronize`, and `reopened`; on `closed` with `merged: true` into `main`, it reruns CI on the exact merged revision with `package_app: true`, then calls CD with `needs: ci` and CI's artifact ID, checksum, and revision outputs. Closed unmerged PRs skip; manual dispatch validates only; there is no sample `push` trigger or push-based deployment. PR heads must belong to the caller repository and calls triggered by `dependabot[bot]` skip. Only CD needs `id-token: write`; CI has no Azure inputs or OIDC permission. CD verifies the same-run package before Azure authentication and does not check out or build application code. The CI table reports CI/image results; CD writes its own health summary. Image publication is controlled by the caller through `publish_image`; the reusable CI publishes after the required gates pass. Container deployment also supports post-merge CI and deployment for the exact merged commit.

`reusable-app-ci-regression.yml` calls that workflow from the same commit against the Python fixture in `tests/consumer-repo/python-app`. It runs for pull requests targeting `main` and manual dispatch. Eligible same-repository pull requests and manual runs publish the scanned image after all required gates pass. When a pull request merges, the caller reruns CI for the exact merge commit and deploys that run's image digest if the Azure variables are configured. Manual dispatch to the actual default branch can also deploy. Its project key is explicitly `Lekanlekzy_stage1-devsecops`, so no project-key variable is needed. Configure the existing `SONAR_TOKEN` secret with analysis permission for that project. The Sonar organization is fixed to `lekanlekzy`. Fork and Dependabot pull requests skip the secret-backed call.

`main-protection.yml.disabled` is intentionally disabled at the user's request. GitHub does not load this filename as a workflow. When activation is requested, restoring the `.yml` extension enables the retained definition for the local contract suite, actionlint, and zizmor on pull requests targeting `main` and pushes to `main`. GitHub rulesets or classic branch protection enforce branch policy separately; remote settings are unchanged.

See `docs/stage-1/reusable-workflow-contract.md`, `docs/stage-1/action-pins.md`, and `docs/stage-1/default-branch-protection.md` for caller requirements, verified tool pins, and repository settings.

## Container deployment to Azure Container Apps

reusable-container-cd.yml accepts the image URI, registry digest, and commit outputs from reusable-app-ci.yml. It authenticates with Azure OIDC, updates a named container through Azure CLI, deploys the immutable image digest, waits for the new revision to provision, and requires /healthz (configurable) to report status ok and the same commit revision. It supports merged pull-request closes for the exact merge commit, plus push or manual dispatch on the caller repository's actual default branch, and requests only id-token: write.

Use examples/caller-workflows/node-container-ci-cd.yml.example as a thin caller. Set SONAR_PROJECT_KEY, SONAR_TOKEN, AZURE_CONTAINER_APP_NAME, AZURE_CONTAINER_NAME, AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID, and AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID. Configure the GitHub non-production Environment and matching Azure federated identity. Provision the Azure Container App with external HTTPS ingress and configure its GHCR pull access before the first deployment. Private GHCR images need a read-only package credential configured on the Container App; no GHCR credential is passed to the workflow. Multiple revision mode deployments switch ingress traffic to latest=100 and replace any existing split. Local contract checks cannot verify Azure OIDC, registry access, GitHub Actions execution, or the running application. See Microsoft's [Azure Container Apps revision documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/revisions).
